# 5. Hits and blocks are identified by byte spans, and blocks form a tree

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-11-11

## Context

A block is a line range plus a copy of its text (`CodeBlock { line_start, line_end, code, .. }`, `types.rs`) and a hit is a whole line (`LineHit { line_number, text }`). Both analyzers hold the exact span when they build a block (`push_block` in `analysis/ts/parse.rs`, `record` in `analysis/rust/parse.rs`) and drop it after cutting lines and `code`. The tree is dropped too: `parent` is a `ParentContext { kind, name }`, not a link to a block.

Later stages re-derive structure from lines or text. Non-test code mentions `line_start`, `line_end`, `matched_lines`, `line_number` or `code` on 87 lines in 11 files. The guessing stages:

- `owned_hits` (`pipeline/mod.rs`) picks a hit's owner by line range, own-text matching, and `outer.code.contains(inner.code)` for equal ranges.
- `snippet` and `signature_shows` (`output/agent.rs`) decide by text whether the signature already shows the first line.
- `encloses_member` and `overlaps_significantly` (`dedup.rs`) compare line ranges, so two disjoint blocks on one line overlap fully.
- `name_match_boost` (`rank/boost.rs`) cuts a signature string at `(`, `<`, `{`, `=`, `:` to recover a name.

The same gap produced 7 fix or test commits in 3 PRs (#66: 3, #68: 1, #77: 3). Ownership was rewritten three times (earliest of equal size, innermost by range, own text on the line) for `} b() {`, `}, // note` and `const a = 1; const needle = 2;`. A test function and its module with the same range were credited twice. A first-line snippet repeated or hid the signature. `pub(crate) fn` was cut to `pub`. `pipeline/proptests.rs` re-implements the old rule as its reference, so it pins the rule, not a contract.

## Decision

We recommend identifying hits and blocks by byte spans and linking blocks into a forest.

- A hit carries its line and the byte range of each match.
- A block carries a byte span and its parent's index in the file's block list, built once by the analyzer.
- The AST supplies `name` and `kind` as typed fields.
- A hit belongs to the innermost block whose span contains the hit's start byte. Equal spans resolve by parent depth, not text.
- Snippets are cut from spans and dedup compares spans.

## Consequences

Deleted: own-text matching and the equal-range rule in `owned_hits`, `signature_shows`, the head-cutting in `name_match_boost` with its `unrestricted` special case, and the proptest's reference reimplementation.

Costs:

- `LineHit` grows a list of match ranges. The searcher does not give them: `SinkMatch` in `grep-searcher` 0.1.17 (`sink.rs:379-423`) exposes only `bytes()`, `absolute_byte_offset()` and `line_number()` for the whole line. In-line offsets need `Matcher::find_iter` (`grep-matcher` 0.1.9, `lib.rs:629`) over each matching line. `LineCollector::text_matches` (`text_search.rs`) already makes that second pass for CRLF lines.
- Offsets must mean the same bytes on both sides. The searcher sees raw file bytes and the analyzer sees the lossy-decoded `String`, which differ after any invalid UTF-8.
- Each block gains a span (16 bytes) and a parent index (4 to 8 bytes). `code` stays, so nested blocks keep duplicating text.
- Dedup compares bytes instead of lines, the one stage whose output can change beyond the old bugs.

## Alternatives considered

Keep line ranges and patch each case, as we did. It costs a commit per new line shape, and each patch adds a rule the next must respect.

## Order of work

Three PRs. After each, `scripts/rg-compare.py` must not drop: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 23/24 and 12/12. Output is byte-identical except the cases the old rules got wrong, which each PR lists.

1. Analyzers emit spans, parent indices, `name` and `kind`. Nothing reads them yet. Tests assert spans slice to `code`.
2. The sink reports match ranges and `owned_hits` becomes innermost-containing. Test-first: the three line shapes above and the same-range test function and module.
3. `snippet`, `name_match_boost` and `dedup_blocks` read spans and typed fields.

## Not measured

Memory and time of the second regex pass and the spans on a large repo. How many harness queries change under byte-based dedup. Whether mapping lossy offsets beats searching decoded text. How many of the 87 sites would change.

## 34. A held-out set and a Rust gate join the harness (2026-11-10)

- **Decision.** Three repositories that no ranking change was tuned on (fastify, trpc, date-fns) carry 24 multi-word and 12 member questions, written and checked with `rg` before monokl first ran on them. They score on their own lines (`held-out questions`, `held-out members`) and the Rust rows on the pinned fd checkout pool into one `--min-rust-recall` rate. The three gates default to 0.9.
- **Why.** The declared-name bonus (§32) was tuned and scored on the same 18 questions, so 17 of 18 was optimistic. The held-out set scored 23 of 24 and 12 of 12 on first run, close to the tuned 17 of 18 and 15 of 16, which is evidence the bonus and member rows generalize. Rust scored 22 of 24 (11 of 13 identifiers, 11 of 11 questions, 11 of 11 members) once the analyzer landed.
- **Rule.** Ranking changes may be tuned on the tuned sets and must be reported on the held-out set. A held-out miss is never fixed by editing the question.
- **Open.** The sets are small, so one miss moves a rate by 4 points; read them as a regression guard, not an estimate. The one held-out miss is trpc `create websocket client` (answer file at rank 7).

## 35. Reads, hit lines and run time have stated bounds (2026-11-11)

Follows [ADR 0004](../adr/0004-search-stays-stateless-and-every-stage-has-a-stated-bound.md) rules 2 to 4 (PR 88).

- **Decision.** Text search reads at most 4 MiB of a file (`MAX_FILE_BYTES`), checked on the open handle. A larger file is skipped unread and reported as one grouped line. A hit line is kept to 4096 bytes (`MAX_LINE_BYTES`) and the cut lines are counted in a warning. `--timeout SECONDS` defaults to 30, accepts fractions, and 0 disables it. It is checked between files in text search and between batches in analysis. Each stage always finishes its first batch, so a tiny timeout still returns something. An expired run prints `partial result: ... expired after searching|analyzing N of M files` and exits 0. `tests/scaling.rs` takes the fastest of 5 runs at 2,500 and 10,000 inputs for rank and dedup, text search and a whole search, and asserts the time ratio stays under 10 (a quadratic step gives 16). It never asserts absolute times.
- **Why.** The limit equals the 4 MiB parse cap, so a larger file could only come back as too large to parse after being read whole. On the PR's measurements a directory of forty 5 MB files peaked at 479 MB and one 300 MB line at 752 MB; both are now about 5 MB.
- **Partial results.** They are the only output that differs between runs, because which files are reached depends on speed. A `-term` exclusion applies only to the files reached. Without a timeout, output is deterministic.
- **Cost of the line cap.** A term that matches only past byte 4096 of a line is not seen by required-term and keyword checks. The warning says so.

## 36. Parse on a fixed stack behind a nesting scan (2026-11-11)

Replaces §23's per-byte stack and its size caps (PR 83).

- **Decision.** Every parse runs on one 256 MiB stack (`PARSE_STACK_BYTES`). A linear scan (`analysis/nesting.rs`) estimates the recursion a file can cause and rejects it before any parser sees it. The cap is 16,384 levels for TypeScript and 256 for Rust. A rejected file is degraded as too deep and named in the diagnostic with its depth and cap. The post-parse tree-depth check and its leaked trees are gone, because no accepted tree is deeper than the drop thread holds. The size cap is 4 MiB (35).
- **Why.** §23's stack grew with the input, so whether a file was analyzed depended on its length and the host's memory. A fixed stack makes cost and outcome a function of the file alone. §23 deleted the scan because it rejected valid files; the scan now errs only upward and is tested against the real parsers.
- **A false rejection, found and fixed.** The first cap (4,096 levels on a 64 MiB stack) rejected a component with 3,000 sibling JSX elements: its true depth is about 3, but closers do not lower the estimate, so it cost about 45,000 units. The cap and the stack grew by 4x together to keep the margin (the worst nesting at the cap needed 96 MiB and overflowed 64 MiB, so 256 MiB is at least 2.6x). End-to-end tests cover 3,000 JSX siblings, a 12,000-term concatenation and a 20,000-row array.
- **Three soundness bugs found by review, fixed.** `for await (` lost its loop head to `await`. A `;` in JSX text reset what the open elements had charged. Each ambiguous `/` rescanned its whole line. Each has a test that parses the input in a child process on a small stack to show the hazard is real.
- **A differential fuzzer.** `soundness_tests.rs` generates nesting-heavy token soups, scans them under a cap scaled to an 8 MiB stack, and parses every accepted input in a child process. An abort is a counterexample. It found more under-estimates, all fixed with regression tests: a template `}` inside a possible regex flipped backtick parity; Rust 2024 `#"` is a prefix, not a string; unterminated strings, templates, comments and raw strings hid the rest of the source; and the Rust cap let trees deeper than the drop thread holds (now 256 levels). On the final code the PR run found no counterexample.
- **Evidence, not proof.** The fuzzer samples inputs; it does not prove the scan never under-estimates. `MONOKL_FUZZ_SECONDS` sets the run length. The estimate stays a deliberate over-estimate wherever the scan cannot tell syntax apart.
- **Open.** A valid file over the cap loses its results and the user sees it by name.

## 37. Deletions of code nothing reads (2026-11-11)

PRs 84 to 87. Each removed code whose only reader was a test or nothing.

- **Decision.** The query module is crate-private, and tests that scanned source text, probed for absent derives or re-checked exhaustiveness are deleted (PR 84). `coverage_boost` is gone (PR 85): every printed block holds a matching line, so it was a constant 1.0, and `finalScore` is 1.0 lower with the order unchanged. The score breakdown fields and `SearchResponse` totals that only tests read are gone, and `SymbolKind` derives `Ord` instead of mirroring it by hand. `--max-bytes`, `Budget.max_bytes`, the `miette` feature and dependency, and `ToonProjection<N>` are gone (PR 86); `render_search` and `search_row_texts` replace the projection, and `apply_budget` takes the printed row texts. Unread analyzer output is gone (PR 87): symbols, dependencies, exports, JSX, `LangData`, the `Digest` and its `blake3` dependency, `AnalysisProfile`, `AnalyzerCapabilities`, `language_for`, `matched_keywords`, `RankedBlock.parent_context` and `ParentContext.line`. `LanguageAnalyzer` is now `languages`, `supports` and `analyze(path, text)`.
- **Why.** Search reads only `blocks`, `test_blocks`, `had_parse_errors` and `degradation`. `--max-tokens` is `ceil(bytes / 3)`, so the 2 MiB byte cap bound only above about 700,000 tokens. CLI errors render through michi's `DomainError`, so the `miette` derives had no use. Unique crates in the workspace tree went from 252 to 232. PR 87 removed 2,440 lines and added 308, and the release binary went from 3,762,592 to 3,696,240 bytes. Output was byte-identical on 101 queries (87) and on 93 comparisons (86; only `search --help` differs).
- **Consequences.** `--max-bytes` is now a usage error (exit 2). A command that needs a removed field restores it with its analyzer output and a reader. [ADR 0002](../adr/0002-digest-lives-in-monokl-until-wisp-contracts.md) stands for whoever re-adds `Digest`. `LanguageId` keeps `TypeScript` and `Rust`.
- **Open.** The `Language`/`LanguageId` unification. The architecture docs still describe `miette` and `max_bytes`.

## 38. Process lessons (2026-11-11)

- **Decision.** Compile and test the combined state before merging a PR that other PRs touch, and run the soundness tests under plain `cargo test` as well as `nextest`.
- **Why.** Two merges broke `main` because each PR passed alone. The object-member score tests (PR 70) were written before the name bonus (§32) and failed once both were in. The scaling test (PR 88) constructed a field that a deletion (PR 85) removed; PR 90 fixed it. CI on a branch checks that branch against the `main` it started from, not against what merges beside it.
- **A real race hid behind one runner.** The soundness tests passed under `nextest` (one process per test) but shared one batch file under `cargo test`, where concurrent child launches overwrote each other's file and removed each other's directory. Each batch now has its own directory (PR 89).

## 39. A block carries the name its analyzer read from the syntax tree (2026-11-12)

- **Decision.** `CodeBlock` gains `name: Option<String>`, filled by both analyzers for every block that declares an identifier, and `name_match_boost` tokenizes it. §32's text-derived name (the signature or first non-comment line, cut at `(`, `<`, `{`, `=` or `:`, with a `pub(crate)` special case for Rust) is deleted. This is the `name` slice of [ADR 0005](../adr/0005-hits-and-blocks-are-identified-by-byte-spans-and-blocks-form-a-tree.md); spans and parent indices stay open.
- **What the name is.** A function, class, interface, type alias, enum, namespace, method, property or constant has its identifier. An `impl` has its target, or `Trait for Target`, the same string its members use as `parent.name`. A member key that is a string literal or a private identifier has its text; a computed key has none. A declaration of several variables takes the first plain identifier. A re-export, an anonymous default export, a destructuring declaration, a macro call and an `extern` block have `None` and get no name boost.
- **Why.** The head of a line is not a name: it held modifiers (`get`, `static`, `default`) and the type of a variable as words, and needed a `pub(crate)` rule because `(` ends the head. The tree has the name.
- **Output.** No column is added. Scores differ only where the old head held a word the name does not (a modifier, or the type of a variable) and for `export default Button;`, which now has no name because it declares none. The harness is unchanged: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 23/24 and 12/12.
- **Not done.** A typed `ParsedTerm` for ranking. `rank_blocks` and `name_match_boost` take BM25 tokens, which are lowercased fragments of the user's words and not query terms, and `ParsedTerm` already types the one place a query term is read (`QueryPlan`). A wrapper around `&str` tokens would add a type with no new check.

## 40. Blocks carry a byte span and a parent index (2026-11-14)

# Contributing

By participating in this project, you agree to abide by the [Code of Conduct](./CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). Found a security issue? See [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md) instead of opening a public issue.

## Setup

[proto](https://moonrepo.dev/proto) pins the toolchain in `.prototools`; [just](https://just.systems) runs every task.

```bash
just setup          # install the pinned Rust and moon, install git hooks
just install-tools  # nextest, llvm-cov, machete, mutants, deny, typos, zizmor
```

| Recipe | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `just ci` | Everything CI runs |
| `just test` | nextest plus doctests |
| `just lint` | `cargo fmt --check` and clippy with `-D warnings`, all features and no default features |
| `just doc-check` | `cargo doc` with warnings as errors |
| `just coverage` | Line coverage, failing below the justfile's threshold |
| `just check-drift` | Fails when a duplicated fact (the Callisto pin) disagrees with its owner |
| `just deny` | Licenses, advisories, bans and sources |
| `just machete` | Unused dependencies |
| `just mutants` | Mutation testing, on demand only |
| `just changeset <bump> "<summary>"` | Record a pending change for the next release (Callisto) |
| `just changesets` | Check Callisto config and pending changesets |

See [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#current-state).

## Proposing a change

- A spec correction: fix the spec file and add a dated entry to `docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`.
- A decision with a credible alternative that is expensive to reverse: write an ADR (`docs/adr/0000-template.md`).

- A change users can see needs a changeset. Internal changes (tests, CI, docs, refactors) do not.

Each changeset becomes one bullet in the changelog. Each version lists its bullets under `Major Changes`, `Minor Changes` and `Patch Changes` headings, below the release date and a compare link. The release PR titles each change by its first line and collapses the rest.

- **Entries appear in filename order within their bump heading.** Prefix a filename with `0-` (then `1-`) to make an entry lead its heading.
- **Put identifiers, flags and syntax in backticks.**

- Open with a bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it, then one line on its value: what they can now do or what changed for them.
- When there is more to say, add short bullets in this order: why it matters, how to adopt it (commands, configuration, migration), and limits they will hit. Use sub-bullets for detail.
- Group a longer entry under bold labels such as **Upgrading** or **Scripting**. Do not use `#` headings; the changelog supplies those.

A removed or renamed flag, a removed or non-public library item, a changed output shape or value and a library signature change are breaking.
- One idea per bullet. Leave out internals unless the user must know them.

## Filing an issue

Say what you expected, what happened, and, if it's a spec-vs-reality mismatch, which file in `docs/spec/` you were reading.
